changed.title: Balanced partitions of endpoint-inconsistent binary paths have two cells per edge and an exact width profile
changed.statement:
∀ (m : ℕ), 0 < m → ∀ f : Fin m → Bool,
  let Cell := Finset (Fin (m+1) × Bool)
  let flip := decide (Odd ((Finset.univ.filter (fun i => f i = true)).card))
  let last := Fin.last m
  let load := fun (L : Finset Cell) (x : Fin (m+1) → Bool) =>
    (L.filter (fun C => (C.filter (fun p => x p.1 ≠ p.2)) = ∅)).card
  let h := Nat.clog 2 m
  ∃ L : Finset Cell, L.card = 2*m ∧
    (∀ C ∈ L,
      (∀ i : Fin (m+1), ¬ ((i, false) ∈ C ∧ (i, true) ∈ C)) ∧
      (∃ a : Bool, (0, a) ∈ C ∧ (last, !(a ^^ flip)) ∈ C) ∧
      (∃ (i : Fin m) (b : Bool), (i.castSucc, b) ∈ C ∧ (i.succ, !(b ^^ f i)) ∈ C) ∧
      (C.card = h+1 ∨ C.card = h+2)) ∧
    (L.filter (fun C => C.card = h+1)).card = 2*(2^h-m) ∧
    (L.filter (fun C => C.card = h+2)).card = 2*(2*m-2^h) ∧
    ∀ x, load L x = if x last = (x 0 ^^ flip) then 0 else 1
changed.unlocks: constructs an exact two-width partition of inconsistent path words, used by both cyclic covers
changed.context: Use a full ordered binary tree with m leaves obtained from the complete tree of height h by collapsing 2^h−m bottom sibling pairs. Its leaves represent edges. Pin inconsistent endpoint values in either orientation. At an internal split read the shared vertex. Exactly one child has inconsistent endpoints, and either child can be selected by one answer. Every selected midpoint is distinct from earlier splits along a branch. The leaves are disjoint, give the two asserted widths, and terminate with a violated edge.

changed.title: For k at least five coprime to three, the largest key flat on which both full one-round output words are affine has dimension floor of k over three
changed.statement:
∀ (k : Nat) (hk : 0 < k), 5 ≤ k → k % 3 ≠ 0 →
  let W := Fin k → ZMod 2
  let ix := fun i : Nat => (⟨i % k, Nat.mod_lt _ hk⟩ : Fin k)
  let rot := fun (s : Nat) (x : W) (i : Fin k) => x (ix (i.val + k - s % k))
  let mix := fun (d : Nat) (x : W) (i : Fin k) =>
    x i + x (ix (i.val + d)) + x (ix (i.val + k - d % k))
  let step := fun (x : W) (i : Fin k) =>
    x i + (1 + x (ix (i.val + 1))) * x (ix (i.val + 2))
  ∀ row col c₁ c₂ : W,
    let out := fun (key : W) =>
      ((step (mix 1 (rot 1 key + row)) + key + c₁,
        step (mix 2 (rot 3 key + col)) + rot 4 key + c₂) : W × W)
    let flat := fun (U : Submodule (ZMod 2) W) (base : W) =>
      ∃ f : U →ₗ[ZMod 2] (W × W), ∀ u : U, out (base + u.val) = out base + f u
    (∀ (U : Submodule (ZMod 2) W) (base : W), flat U base →
      Module.finrank (ZMod 2) U ≤ k / 3) ∧
    ∃ U : Submodule (ZMod 2) W, Module.finrank (ZMod 2) U = k / 3 ∧ ∀ base, flat U base
changed.unlocks: prices affine restrictions for simultaneous linearization of both full one-round words
changed.context: Write a_i for the row coordinate forms on U. The column forms are b_i=a_(i-1)+a_i+a_(i+1), up to rotation. Adjacent nonzero forms in either list must agree. Group equal nonzero labels across zeros. Between different labels two zeros give unequal adjacent b values. At a one-zero gap the sum of both labels forces each boundary run to have length at least two. Each group with its outgoing gap costs at least three sites. Use equal-label pairs with one zero between pairs and lengthen one pair for the remainder. Gate-price companions cannot exist for a maximum affine dimension.

changed.title: Binary Nullstellensatz degree for Horn implications with two endpoints fixed by one allowed pair
changed.statement:
∀ (n d : ℕ) (s t : Fin n), s ≠ t →
  ∀ pred : Fin n → Finset (Fin n), (∀ v, v ≠ s → v ∉ pred v) →
  let P := MvPolynomial (Fin n) (ZMod 2)
  let static := fun (axioms : Finset (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n))) (budget : ℕ) =>
    ∃ (q : PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n) → P) (b : Fin n → P),
      (∀ C ∈ axioms, q C = 0 ∨ (q C).totalDegree + (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.clausePoly C).totalDegree ≤ budget) ∧
      (∀ v, b v = 0 ∨ (b v).totalDegree + 2 ≤ budget) ∧
      axioms.sum (fun C => q C * PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.clausePoly C) +
        (∑ v, b v * (MvPolynomial.X v * MvPolynomial.X v + MvPolynomial.X v)) = 1
  let clause := fun v : Fin n =>
    insert (v,true) ((pred v).image (fun u => (u,false)))
  let pins : Finset (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n)) :=
    {{(t,true),(s,true)}, {(t,false),(s,true)}, {(t,false),(s,false)}}
  let F := (Finset.univ.erase s).image clause ∪ pins
  let enabled := fun (z : Option (Fin n)) (current : Finset (Option (Fin n))) =>
    z = none ∨ ∃ i : Fin n, z = some i ∧
      ((i = s ∧ none ∈ current) ∨ (i ≠ s ∧ ∀ u ∈ pred i, some u ∈ current))
  let up := fun A B : Finset (Option (Fin n)) => B.card ≤ d ∧
    ∃ z, z ∉ A ∧ B = insert z A ∧ enabled z A
  static F d ↔
    ∃ S : Finset (Fin n), t ∈ S ∧ (S.card < d ∨ s ∈ S) ∧
      Relation.ReflTransGen (fun U V => up U V ∨ up V U) ∅ (S.image some)
changed.unlocks: converts a static refutation with a paired source and sink into a terminal pebbling and conversely
changed.context: Expand each bounded-degree cofactor in monomials and take squarefree supports on the cube. Interior rules toggle a vertex with its parents present. For any external support of size at most d-2, the three endpoint polynomials span a source toggle and the two sink monomials, with or without the source. One extra predecessor enforces the lost source slot. The empty component must meet an allowable sink monomial. Conversely sum the formal edge identities along a path and add its terminal monomial. The budget permits all cofactors.

changed.title: Which prescribed pairwise witnesses extend to exact three-owner ternary CNFs for physical cyclic window feasibility
changed.statement:
∀ (n w : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (owner : Fin n → Fin 3),
  let Word := Fin n → Bool
  let Pattern := Fin (w+1) → Bool
  let pos := fun (r : Fin n) (d : Fin (w+1)) =>
    (⟨(r.val + d.val) % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩ : Fin n)
  let window := fun (x : Word) (r : Fin n) (d : Fin (w+1)) => x (pos r d)
  (∀ (party : Fin 3) (z : Fin n), ∃ r : Fin n, owner r = party ∧
    ∃ d : Fin (w+1), pos r d = z) →
  ∀ (k : Fin 3 → ℕ) (ternary : Bool),
    let next := fun e : Fin 3 => e + 1
    let Msg := (e : Fin 3) → Fin (k e) → Bool
    let Table := Fin n → Pattern → Bool
    let pins := fun (word : Word) (row : Fin n) (pat : Pattern) => decide (pat = window word row)
    let V := fun (p : Fin 3) (q : ℕ) =>
      Sum ({r : Fin n // owner r = p} × Pattern)
        (Sum ((e : {t : Fin 3 // t = p ∨ next t = p}) × Fin (k e.val)) (Fin q))
    ∀ code : Word → Msg,
      (∃ (priv : Fin 3 → ℕ) (F : (p : Fin 3) → Finset (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (V p (priv p)))),
        let accepts := fun (tab : Table) (y : Msg) => ∀ p : Fin 3, ∃ a : Fin (priv p) → Bool,
          PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Satisfies
            (Sum.elim (fun h : {i : Fin n // owner i = p} × Pattern => tab h.1.val h.2)
              (Sum.elim (fun bit : (e : {t : Fin 3 // t = p ∨ next t = p}) × Fin (k e.val) =>
                y bit.1.val bit.2) a)) (↑(F p) : Set _)
        (ternary = true → ∀ p, ∀ C ∈ F p, C.card ≤ 3) ∧
        (∀ T : Table, (∃ x : Word, ∀ i, T i (window x i) = true) ↔ ∃ transcript, accepts T transcript) ∧
        ∀ x : Word, accepts (pins x) (code x)) ↔
      ∀ chosen : Fin 3 → Word,
        (∀ e : Fin 3, code (chosen e) e = code (chosen (next e)) e) →
        ∀ party : Fin 3, chosen party = chosen 0
changed.unlocks: characterizes the channel selections that extend to a local ternary encoding
changed.context: For each word give every row its unique window of that word and use the prescribed accepting transcript. If the three owners choose words agreeing on the transcript of each shared channel, splice their rows and private witnesses. Every owner sees every physical position, so feasibility forces all three words equal. Conversely each owner guesses a word, checks its own rows and its two channel values against the code. Three passing guesses coincide by hypothesis. Encode these finite local tests by CNFs with private ternary gates.

changed.title: Exact deterministic query depth for finding a violated signed graph edge with arbitrary initially known vertex bits
changed.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → ∀ E : Fin n → Fin n → Bool → Prop,
  (∀ u v b, E u v b → E v u b) → (∀ u b, ¬ E u u b) →
  ∀ (S : Finset (Fin n)) (z : Fin n → Bool) (d : ℕ),
    let walk := fun (m : ℕ) (v : ℕ → Fin n) (s : ℕ → Bool) =>
      ∀ i < m, E (v i) (v (i+1)) (s i)
    let parity := fun (m : ℕ) (s : ℕ → Bool) =>
      decide (Odd (((Finset.range m).filter (fun i => s i = true)).card))
    (∃ ask : List Bool → Fin n,
      ∀ (x : Fin n → Bool) (ans : Fin d → Bool), (∀ i ∈ S, x i = z i) →
        let queried := fun i : Fin d => ask ((List.ofFn ans).take i.val)
        (∀ i, ans i = x (queried i)) →
        let seen := S ∪ Finset.univ.image queried
        ∃ u ∈ seen, ∃ v ∈ seen, ∃ b : Bool, E u v b ∧ x v ≠ (x u ^^ b)) ↔
    (∃ (m : ℕ) (v : ℕ → Fin n) (s : ℕ → Bool), 1 ≤ m ∧ m ≤ 2^d ∧
      walk m v s ∧ v 0 ∈ S ∧ v m ∈ S ∧ z (v m) ≠ (z (v 0) ^^ parity m s)) ∨
    (0 < d ∧ ∃ (m : ℕ) (v : ℕ → Fin n) (s : ℕ → Bool), 1 ≤ m ∧
      2*m ≤ 2^d ∧ walk m v s ∧ v 0 = v m ∧ parity m s = true)
changed.unlocks: determines how many vertex queries suffice to exhibit a violated signed edge with any initial pins
changed.context: Bisect a contradicting walk between pinned endpoints. On a closed odd walk, query its base vertex. Conversely, if neither short witness exists, answer any next query to respect all walks of length at most 2^(d−1) from old pins to the queried vertex. Opposite demands would concatenate to an old contradiction of length at most 2^d. A short closed walk at the queried vertex is excluded separately. Induct on the remaining depth. With zero queries a violated edge requires a contradicting length-one walk between given pins.
changed.sketch: Bisect a contradicting walk between pinned endpoints. On a closed odd walk, query its base vertex. Conversely, if neither short witness exists, answer any next query to respect all walks of length at most 2^(d−1) from old pins to the queried vertex. Opposite demands would concatenate to an old contradiction of length at most 2^d. A short closed walk at the queried vertex is excluded separately. Induct on the remaining depth. With zero queries a violated edge requires a contradicting length-one walk between given pins.
